Practised finding partners that make 100 using tens numbers and number-line jumps.
Answered 30 + 70 = 100 correctly.
Used jumps from 80 to 100 to explain 20; counted two jumps of 10.
Answered 46 to 50 as 4 after reconsidering.
75’s partner for 100 remained unresolved by the end of the lesson.
end.parentNote: Vihaan practised making 100 with tens and showing the difference using jumps on a number line. They explained 80 + 20 by counting two jumps of 10 and corrected the 46-to-50 response during the lesson. The 75 problem was still confusing at the end; at home, practise pairs such as 70 + 30, 80 + 20, and 75 + 25 with a number line.
